content.title: Form Submission: One Source of Truth
content.hook: When a normal HTML form is submitted, the browser may perform its default submission behavior.
goals: Handle React form submission with controlled fields and prevent unwanted browser navigation when the application should handle the submission itself.

content.question: What does `event.preventDefault()` do in this example?

options.text: It prevents the form's default browser submission behavior so the React handler can handle the submission.
It prevents the user from typing.

feedback.correct: `preventDefault()` controls the browser's default action for this event. It does not stop your handler from running.
feedback.incorrect: `preventDefault()` controls the browser's default action for this event. It does not stop your handler from running.

content.title: Build the smallest form
Why submit instead of click?
content.text:
Suppose the user types a query and presses Enter while focused in the input.

A form's `onSubmit` handler represents the form action more accurately than attaching the behavior only to one particular button click.

The interaction is about submitting the form, not merely clicking one element.

content.title: Validate before acting

activities.title: Do not store what you can derive

content.title: Do not store what you can derive
content.text:
Suppose the UI needs to show: ```text Search: forge Length: 5 ``` You do not need both `query` and `queryLength` as separate state. ```jsx

Search: {query}

Length: {query.length}

``` The length is derived from the current query.

content.question: Which design creates the fewest competing facts?

options.text: `query` state plus `queryLength` state plus a second variable that mirrors both
Store the query only in the button
Store the query only in the submit event object

feedback.correct: Keep the source fact in state. Calculate dependent values when rendering unless a separate source of truth is genuinely required.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the source fact in state. Calculate dependent values when rendering unless a separate source of truth is genuinely required.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A controlled form keeps input state in React, then an event handler decides what a submission should do.
**Senior habit:** Separate three questions: “What value do we have?”, “What does the user intend?”, and “What should happen because of that intent?”
nextSteps: Build a controlled form, prevent the default browser submission, and derive a display value from the single source of truth.
